stem: A weak acid HA has degree of dissociation $x$. Which option gives the correct expression of $(\text{pH}-\text{p}K_a)$?

steps.text: $K_a=\frac{[\text{H}^+][\text{A}^-]}{[\text{HA}]}$, so $\text{pH}=\text{p}K_a+\log\frac{[\text{A}^-]}{[\text{HA}]}$.

stem: Given below is the plot of the molar conductivity vs $\sqrt{\text{concentration}}$ for KCl in aqueous solution. The plot is a straight line: $\Lambda_m=150$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt C=0.10$ (mol/L)$^{1/2}$ and $\Lambda_m=100$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt C=0.15$ (mol/L)$^{1/2}$. If, for the higher concentration of KCl solution, the resistance of the conductivity cell is $100\ \Omega$, then the resistance of the same cell with the dilute solution is $x\ \Omega$. The value of $x$ is ______ (Nearest integer)

steps.text: Higher concentration: $\sqrt C=0.15$, so $C=0.0225$ M and $\Lambda_m=100$. Dilute: $\sqrt C=0.10$, so $C=0.01$ M and $\Lambda_m=150$.
$\kappa=\frac{\Lambda_mC}{1000}$ and $R\propto\frac1\kappa$ for the same cell.
$\frac{R_{dil}}{R_{conc}}=\frac{100\times0.0225}{150\times0.01}=1.5$, so $R_{dil}=150\ \Omega$.
